title: Mercury and the Man Bitten by an Ant
attribution: Excerpted verbatim from Aesop's Fables, translated by V. S. Vernon Jones (1912), via Project Gutenberg.
body: A Man once saw a ship go down with all its crew, and commented severely on the injustice of the gods. "They care nothing for a man's character," said he, "but let the good and the bad go to their deaths together." There was an ant-heap close by where he was standing, and, just as he spoke, he was bitten in the foot by an Ant. Turning in a temper to the ant-heap he stamped upon it and crushed hundreds of unoffending ants. Suddenly Mercury appeared, and belaboured him with his staff, saying as he did so, "You villain, where's your nice sense of justice now?"

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what did the Man see happen to a ship?
options: It sailed safely into harbor
It went down with all its crew
It was struck by lightning
It was captured by pirates

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does the Man say the gods let happen together?
options: The good and the bad go to their deaths together
The rich and the poor prosper together
The wise and the foolish suffer together
The young and the old grow old together

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what happened to the Man just as he finished speaking?
options: He was bitten in the foot by an Ant
He was struck by a falling branch
He slipped and fell into the sea
He was approached by a stranger

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what did the Man do to the ant-heap?
options: He walked carefully around it
He stamped upon it and crushed hundreds of unoffending ants
He covered it with a stone
He poured water over it

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what did Mercury do to the Man?
options: He praised his sense of justice
He belaboured him with his staff
He turned him into an ant
He warned him and let him go

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does "unoffending" mean in "crushed hundreds of unoffending ants"?
options: Having done nothing wrong or harmful
Extremely aggressive
Already dead
Hiding from danger

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, why does Mercury ask the Man, "where's your nice sense of justice now?"
options: The Man just condemned the gods for indiscriminate harm, yet did the same to innocent ants out of anger
The Man had earlier promised to protect the ant-heap
Mercury believes the Man never had any sense of justice at all
The Man had asked Mercury to judge the shipwreck's fairness

questions.prompt: Which statement best captures the point of the fable?
options: Those who condemn unfairness in others often act unfairly themselves when provoked
Gods always punish wrongdoing swiftly and visibly
Ants are more dangerous than they appear
Shipwrecks are always caused by divine injustice

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what did the Man comment on after seeing the shipwreck?
options: The injustice of the gods
The cruelty of the sea
The bravery of the sailors
The cost of building ships

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does the Man say the gods care nothing for?
options: A man's wealth
A man's character
A man's family
A man's age

questions.prompt: According to the passage, where was the ant-heap located?
options: Far from where the Man was standing
Close by where the Man was standing
Inside the Man's house
On the deck of the sunken ship

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does "belaboured" mean in "belaboured him with his staff"?
options: Praised repeatedly
Struck or beat repeatedly
Questioned gently
Ignored completely

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, what is ironic about the Man's reaction to being bitten?
options: He forgave the Ant that bit him
He harmed many innocent ants for the act of just one, the very unfairness he had condemned in the gods
He blamed Mercury for the ant bite
He refused to react at all, proving his own fairness

questions.prompt: Which of these best summarizes what happens in the passage?
options: A Man condemns the gods for treating the innocent and guilty alike, then does the same to innocent ants and is punished by Mercury for his hypocrisy
A Man is rescued by Mercury after being bitten by an Ant
A Man learns to respect ants after seeing a shipwreck
Mercury punishes an Ant for biting an innocent Man
